subject: Startups
title: Wrigley: Soap to Chewing Gum
description: A micro-lesson that makes Wrigley: Soap to Chewing Gum usable.

hook.text: William Wrigley Jr. came to Chicago in 1891 to sell soap. He gave away baking powder as a bonus gift.

buildup.text: Customers loved the baking powder more than the soap. So he pivoted to selling baking powder instead.

discovery.text: He offered chewing gum with each baking powder purchase. Again, the freebie became more popular than the product.

twist.text: Wrigley pivoted a second time—from baking powder to gum. The free gift beat the main product twice in a row.

climax.text: Wrigley's became the world's largest gum company, worth billions. Three pivots chased what customers actually wanted.

punchline.text: He followed the freebie. It led to a billion-dollar brand.

quiz.question: What did Wrigley originally sell before chewing gum?
